utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good afternoon, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Welcome to the New York City Council hearing on the Committee on Public Safety.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, please silence all electronics and do not approach the dais.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, if you are test flying today, make sure you ensure that you have filled out a slip at the back of the room.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Any other questions or concerns, please reach a sergeant at arms.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff

chapters.summary: Chair Feliz welcomes committee members, Public Advocate Williams, and outlines the hearing's purpose: examining NYPD crime statistics, celebrating progress on shootings and murders at historic lows, and identifying areas needing attention.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz welcomes members and outlines hearing purpose

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Oswald Feliz, Chair of the Committee on Public Safety.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I want to welcome everyone to today's hearing on NYPD crime statistics.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I also want to welcome committee members who have joined, including Councilmembers Hanks, Banks, Nurse, Areola, Wong.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I also want to welcome our public advocate, Jumanji Williams.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: The Public Safety Committee is holding today's hearing to take a comprehensive look at the areas of public safety that have seen progress.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: We've made a lot of progress these past few years, including on the issue of shootings and murders.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: They're currently at historic lows.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: This is something that we have to celebrate and recognize.

chapters.summary: Feliz highlights that while shootings and murders are at historic lows, felony assaults are drastically up compared to pre-pandemic years—21,500 year-to-date versus 15,000 in 2019—and grand larceny auto has also surged.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz highlights progress on shootings but rising felony assaults vs pre-pandemic

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: One, examine the areas that have seen progress.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: We also want to take a look at crime categories that require attention.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: We've again made a lot of progress on issues related to shootings and murders.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: But when we look at the crime statistics from 2019, the pre-pandemic years, it is clear there's still room for significant progress.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: This is true for many crime categories, including and especially felonies.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Felony assaults are drastically up compared to the pre-pandemic years, 2017, 2018, and 2019.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: If my math is correct, if my reading of the Comstat report is correct, we've had so far 21.5 thousand felony assaults this year, year to date, versus about 15,000.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: 21.5 versus 15,000 year to date in 2019.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: The same is true for many other crime categories, including grand larceny involving a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: We want to better understand the challenges and discuss what more can be done to address these challenges effectively.

chapters.summary: Feliz states the goal of holding annual crime statistics hearings, thanks NYPD officers for their sacrifices, emphasizes public safety as a shared responsibility, and acknowledges committee staff including Josh Kingsley, Chad Benjamin, Esperanza Diaz, and Santiago Bayan.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz thanks NYPD, acknowledges staff, and sets hearing goals

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: And of course, our goal is to have a hearing like this.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Before the end of every year.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Look at the areas that we've made progress, but also think about the challenges that we have and think about ways and steps that we can take to help resolve those challenges.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: We are thankful for the work and sacrifices of police officers, the work and sacrifices that they make every single day to keep our city safe.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Public safety is a shared responsibility.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: We achieve it with good schools, good jobs, and strong communities.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Police officers play an important role on this issue.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: They help ensure that residents can engage in these activities, work, school, opportunity, without having to worry about their safety, and we are thankful for that.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Their dedication and commitment to the city does not go unnoticed.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I want to thank members of the NYPD and all stakeholders who are testifying today.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Welcome back to City Hall, the People's House.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I would like to thank my staff and committee staff for their hard work.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Josh Kingsley, Senior Counsel to the Committee.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Chad Benjamin, Policy Analyst.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Esperanza Diaz, my Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: And Santiago Bayan, my Legislative Director.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: And many others who have joined, including I see Nini from my team.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I look forward to productive discussion on what's going well, but also the challenges that remain and steps that we can take to help resolve these challenges.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Now I want to briefly pass it on to our very own public advocate, Jumaane Williams.

chapters.summary: Public Advocate Jumaane Williams celebrates NYC's safest summer on record for shootings and murders, notes major crime down 6.2% year-to-date, and highlights that NYC remains one of the safest large cities in the U.S.
chapters.title: Public Advocate Williams celebrates historic crime declines

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Chair, and this is an extremely important hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: I think the public is very concerned about public safety, and media is not helpful as they often warp what's going on to a doomsday scenario unnecessarily.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: So data from the NYPD is really, really important for the public to see.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: As I mentioned, my name is Jermaine Williams, public advocate for the city of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Again, thank you, Chair Feliz and members of the Committee on Public Safety, for holding this important hearing and for the administration and PD for being here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Mayor Mumdani and NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch recently reported that New York City had its safest summer on record for shootings and murders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: That is an absolute applause line.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: That is awesome.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: According to the recently released data, major crime is down 6.2% year-to-date, or about 5,000 fewer crimes are reported citywide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Additionally, there were no reported murders in the subway or NYCHA developments in the time period reported.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: This is consistent with the larger trend that we have seen since the pandemic era spike in crime.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Most major crimes have fallen and have continued to fall since 2020.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: And New York City is still and has been one of the safest large cities in the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: This is something to celebrate.

chapters.summary: Williams discusses difficulties in accurately reporting crime statistics, noting how crime classifications change over time, the 2024 expansion of rape definitions, and concerns that reported declines may be revised after audits.
chapters.title: PA Williams on challenges in accurate crime reporting and data revisions

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: At the same time, this has not captured a full picture of crime in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: It is often difficult to accurately report crime statistics because how crimes are described and how people report them change frequently.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: An assault or shooting could, for example, become a homicide days or weeks later if the victim dies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: A reported burglary could turn out to be a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: In 2024, New York State expanded its definition of rape, which likely contributed to a rise in reported rapes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Certain crimes like rape are chronically underreported, so statistics do not present a full picture.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: It is important to remember that the announcements are falling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Crime rates capture the numbers in that moment, and the decline may decrease or even reverse once the department audits them in the months that follows.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: More concerningly, we understand that those reports may not be updated with the new numbers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: If they are, I'd like to hear that they are.

chapters.summary: Williams criticizes the continuation of broken windows policing under the Mamdani administration, citing a 3,000% increase in court cases for taking up more than one subway seat and a 29% jump in criminal summonses in early 2026.
chapters.title: PA Williams criticizes broken windows policing resurgence and summons surge

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: It is also important to remember that policing tactics purported to achieve these declining reported crime rates can disproportionately harm the most vulnerable New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Under the previous mayor, the NYPD cracking down on low-level quality of life crimes such as taking up more than one seat on the subway and drinking in public.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: This has continued under the Mamdani administration and has been criticized as a resurgence of broken windows policing, at least broken windows adjacent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Broken windows policing is a debunked theory that strict enforcement on low-level crimes will deter more serious crimes later.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Last year, court cases on top charges of taking up more than one seat on the subway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: increased 3,000% compared to the previous year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: In the first three months of 2026, criminal summonses jumped 29%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: A recent analysis of the data by Gothamist found that almost half of civil summonses are tossed by oath, largely attributed to the practice of issuing handwritten tickets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Though they are not criminal summonses, this raises questions about the efficiency of this crackdown on low-level offenses, especially at a time when any contact with the courts puts a non-citizen at risk of detention.

chapters.summary: Williams raises concerns about criminal summonses for cyclists disproportionately affecting people of color, praises the Mamdani administration's plan to end criminal enforcement for e-bike riders, and notes rising shootings in Bronx North despite overall Bronx crime decline.
chapters.title: PA Williams on cyclist summonses and Bronx North shooting increase

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Criminal summonses for cyclists were especially harmful, with 91% of those receiving them were people of more color.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: I am glad that the Mondani administration has announced a plan to end criminal enforcement against e-bikes, riders, and cyclists for low-level traffic offenses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: I want to make sure that doesn't mean there shouldn't be any accountability for infractions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Additionally, Politico reported that the Office of Community Safety met with Bronx elected officials about rising murders and shootings in the Bronx North.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: A new patrol command, which encompasses half of the borough, compared to the same time last year, the Northern Command has seen a nearly 20% increase in shootings and a 6% rise in murders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: However, these crime rates are falling in Bronx South.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Crime in the borough as a whole is trending downward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: This underscores the way we report crimes matters, crime rates matters, and can sometimes obfuscate neighbors that need more attention than this department can provide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: We must ensure that we are not sweeping people into the criminal legal system when they clearly need our direct connection to services and support for stabilization.

chapters.summary: Williams recounts the case of a pregnant woman who gave birth in handcuffs after being taken into custody, argues arrests alone cannot solve inequities, and calls for joint efforts between NYPD and community safety organizations beyond gun violence.
chapters.title: PA Williams calls for collaboration over criminalization and joint safety efforts

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Officers have discretion to issue people summonses instead of taking them into custody, but there are many cases we have seen where they are not using it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: In May, a pregnant woman was taken into custody for drug possession and trespassing and ended up giving birth in a courtroom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Witnesses stated that they gave birth in handcuffs, which is obviously unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Though it's important for people to not only be safe, but to feel safe, we cannot just simply try to punish our way up to safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: We know arrests alone do not solve long and transient inequities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: How the department approaches collaboration has a direct impact on our ability to achieve a citywide level of safety that we can all be proud of.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: I do believe what we're doing on gun violence is a joint effort.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: We're seeing a lot of fruits there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: I'd love to see some kind of joint efforts on the other things as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: And I'm hoping we don't hear about bail and raised age because there are other counties that actually see declines are using the same laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: And there are other spaces in the country that have even seen larger declines with similar laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: So I'm looking forward to a robust conversation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jumaane Williams
utterances.text: Thank you again.

chapters.summary: Feliz emphasizes that 40% of the city's murders, shooting incidents, and shooting victims this year have occurred in the Bronx, underscoring the need to focus public safety discussions on that borough.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz emphasizes Bronx concentration of shootings and murders

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you so much, public advocate.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I just want to briefly emphasize a point made by our public advocate.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: The Bronx has obviously been historically a challenging borough in our city on the issue of crime.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: And for that reason, we can't talk about public safety and crime in our city without putting an emphasis on the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: And if my reading of the comp stat number is correct,

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: 40% of the shootings and 40% of the shooting victims and 40% of the shooting incidents have been in the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Out of all the incidents that we've had related to murders, shooting incidents and victims, about 40% of each of those have been in the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: So we look forward to...

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Having talking about

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: steps we could take to make progress on that issue.

chapters.summary: Feliz recognizes Councilmember Caban on Zoom, introduces NYPD witnesses Deputy Commissioner Michael Gerber and Inspector William Hout, and committee staff administers the oath to testify truthfully.
chapters.title: Introductions and swearing-in of NYPD witnesses

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I also want to recognize Councilmember Caban, who has joined via Zoom, and want to welcome Michael Gerber, Deputy Commissioner of Legal Matters of the Police Department, and also Inspector William Hout, Commanding Officer of the Office of Crime Control Strategies.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: And I'll pass it to the Committee Council for the old.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Can you just affirm to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, and to answer honestly to Councilmember questions?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Inspector Hout reports the fewest year-to-date murders, shooting incidents, and shooting victims in over 30 years of CompStat tracking, with murders down 24.1% and shooting incidents down 9.6%.
chapters.title: Inspector Hout testifies on historic lows in murders and shootings

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair for Lees and members of the Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: My name is Inspector William Hout.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: I'm the commanding officer of the NYPD's Office of Crime Control Strategies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: I am joined here today by Deputy Commissioner of Legal Matters, Michael Gerber.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: On behalf of Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch, we thank you for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: The Office of Crime Control Strategies tracks and analyzes crime across the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Using data-driven approach, we develop strategies to reduce crime and enhance public safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Through the end of August, we have seen the fewest year-to-date murders, shooting incidents, and shooting victims in New York City since we started systematically tracking the data over 30 years ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We have had a 24.1% decrease in murders from last year, 18 fewer murders than the previous record low.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: And we are on track to shatter the record lows of gun violence that we set just last year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Year to date, shooting incidents have decreased 9.6% and shooting victims by 11.9%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: That means 46 fewer shootings and 73 fewer people shot.

chapters.summary: Hout details major crime down 6.2% citywide, with decreases in auto theft (12.8%), robbery (11.9%), burglary (13.9%), and grand larceny (5%), representing about 5,000 fewer index crimes.
chapters.title: Hout on major crime decreases across categories

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: It can be easy to get lost in the statistics and percentages, but we cannot forget these numbers represent real lives saved.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Major crime across the city has decreased 6.2% compared to last year.

chapters.summary: Hout highlights the safest summer for gun violence in NYC history during unprecedented events including NBA Finals, World Cup, and SAIL 250, with 195 shooting incidents and 66 murders from June to August.
chapters.title: Hout on summer safety success during major events

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: This includes a 12.8% decrease in auto theft, an 11.9% decrease in robbery, a 13.9% decrease in burglary, and a 5% decrease in grand larceny.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: I want to highlight this recent summer months.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: There was an unprecedented series of high profile events, including the NBA finals, the World Cup, SAIL 250, and the largest Fourth of July celebration in the nation, all of which put a tremendous demands on the OYPD.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: But we kept our focus on fighting crime, and the results speak for themselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Whether measured by shooting incidents, shooting victims, or murders, this was the safest summer for gun violence in New York City's recorded history.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: From June 1st to August 31st, there were 195 shooting incidents, 32 fewer from the previous record low set in 2025.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: 249 shooting victims, 44 fewer than the previous record low set in 2018, and 66 murders, 12 fewer than the previous record low set in 2017.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We achieved this success because of the work done every day by the men and women of the NYPD.

chapters.summary: Hout describes the department's data-driven precision policing strategy, including summer violence reduction zones that are continuously evaluated and redefined based on crime data, with plans for a winter violence reduction plan.
chapters.title: Hout on precision policing and violence reduction zones

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: They are standing on foot posts in the heat and in the cold, in the middle of the night and on holidays, dedicating their lives and at times risking their lives to keep the people of New York City safe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: They are carrying out the department's data-driven precision policing strategy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: That strategy includes carefully analyzing crime trends to make disciplined, granular deployment decisions, placing officers where they need to be when they're needed most.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We do this systematically through violence reduction zones.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: For example, beginning May 4th, the department launched a summer reduction violence plan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We identified the times and locations where violence is most concentrated during the summer months and surge resources accordingly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Now that the summer has concluded, we are looking ahead to the winter violence reduction plan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We will again define high crime winter zones and deploy additional resources to those areas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: The zones are not static.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We continuously evaluate the data and reassess strategy.

chapters.summary: Hout addresses increases in felony assault (driven by domestic violence at 40% and assaults on public employees up 50%) and rape (up 3.2%), noting 263 individuals arrested three or more times for felony assault, a 205% increase from 2018.
chapters.title: Hout on felony assault and rape increases, recidivism data

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: When the data suggests the highest crime areas are changing, we redefine our zones accordingly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We are proud of our crime fighting successes, but there is more work to do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: In particular, there are two major crime categories that have seen increases this year, felony assault and rape.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Felony assaults are up slightly this year and have been increasing for the past several years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Approximately 40% of felony assaults are acts of domestic violence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: At Police Commissioner's direction, we have overhauled our approach to domestic violence cases through Domestic Violence Unit, enhancing training, streamlining investigations, and working closely with advocacy groups on behalf of survivors of domestic violence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: The increase in felony assaults year to date has been substantially driven by assaults on public service employees.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: More than 50% increase in such assaults compared to the same time last year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: More broadly, we have seen a substantial increase in felony assault recidivism.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: The NYPD has made arrests in nearly 80% of felony assault cases this year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: But as of the end of August, a total of 263 individuals have been arrested three or more times for felony assaults, an increase of 205% compared with 2018.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Reports of rape have increased 3.2% this year through August.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: This may reflect an increase in reporting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: There is a long history of rapes being underreported, and the department is working hard to encourage survivors to speak with us and to provide them with the support when they do so.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We must close the gap between sexual violence that is occurring and sexual violence that is reported, and we are working towards that goal every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to speak with you today, and we are looking forward to answering any questions you may have.

chapters.summary: Feliz asks what policies historically brought down shootings and murders from 2,262 in 1990 to historic lows. Gerber credits CompStat innovation, precision deployment, crew takedowns, and getting illegal guns off the street.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz asks NYPD about historical crime decline factors

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony and again for joining today.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: So I want to start today's conversation by, I guess, looking at the history of the issue.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: So we've obviously made a lot of progress, and especially on the issue of murders and shootings historically.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I was looking at Comstat.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Back in the 90s, we would average about 2,200 murders per year in the city.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: About 2,200 murders in 1990, 2,262 in 1990 to be specific, and our city was able to bring that down by about 80% eight years later, 629 versus 2,262.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: This is something that we must obviously celebrate.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: This year we've been able to drastically bring that down about 30 years later.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Bia, talk to us about those numbers.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: What are policies that you think you would say have historically helped bring specifically the shootings and the murders down in the city?

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: All factors including economic factors, social factors, we know what happened during the pandemic, the coronavirus pandemic, the numbers ballooned, policing strategies, and anything else.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So we all start and then Inspector Howell will take over.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So obviously a very broad question, lots to say on that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: I think for starters,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: You know, you talk about the Comstat era, and you think about what, you know, at the time was a tremendous innovation back in the early 90s.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Now it seems obvious.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: But the concept of put the cops where the crime is when the crime is occurring.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And again, I think that seems obvious today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: It was not obvious then.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And the innovation of having a board that shows where the crime is and this idea of putting thumbtacks on the board.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Okay, here's where the crime is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Here's where we're going to put the cops.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: You know, that idea, that concept, through CompStat and otherwise, I think has dramatically, had a dramatic effect when it comes to murders and shootings and shooting victims, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Because we've gotten better and better at this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So again, it started back in the day as Jack Maple working on a hard copy board with thumbtacks, and we've been able to refine that more and more and more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Precision, precision, precision.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Where precisely is the crime occurring?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Precisely what crimes?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Precisely when?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Are we putting cops where they need to be when they need to be?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Holding commanders accountable to make sure they are doing that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And particularly when it comes to...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Gun violence, often crew related, sometimes drug related, but these are things that are going to be, you know, they're going to be, oh, this is happening in a particular area, a particular crew beef, a particular drug beef.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: If we put the cops in the right place at the right time,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: we can actually prevent gun violence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And you've seen tremendous success with that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Just a few other things before I turn it over to Inspector Hout.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: I think one thing that we've done a tremendous amount of work on are the crew takedowns, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: A relatively small number of people in the city drive gun violence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And so you want to have a really targeted approach, okay, identifying those individuals who are driving the gun violence, devoting resources, working with our DA partners to do successful cases against those individuals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: I mean, getting guns off the street, obviously incredibly important.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Get guns off the street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Getting illegal guns off the street is going to mean fewer shootings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: That is certainly just one part of the answer, but I'll turn it over to Inspector Hebb.

chapters.summary: Hout details current record-low murder (173, down 24%) and shooting numbers, highlights Bronx leading the city in crime reduction at 11.9%, and explains the creation of two patrol boroughs in the Bronx for more resources and oversight.
chapters.title: Hout details current murder/shooting stats and Bronx patrol borough split

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So what we've done, our success is not by accident.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: It's data-driven.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: It's based on precision policing and deployment and making changes rapidly when we need to make them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So just looking at murders, we'll start with that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Year to date, we have read 173 murders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: That's the lowest in the CompStat era.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: That's down 24%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Domestic violence murders are down 22%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: That's tied for the lowest with 2007.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: The borough of Manhattan only saw two murders in August and the fewest murders year to date with 19.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: There was zero housing murders in August.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: That's only occurred one other time in 2024.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So with shootings and shooting victims, the city has historic lows.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: In August and year to date with shooting incidents and shooting victims.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: 442 shooting incidents, that's the lowest in the CompSAT history.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: 538 shooting victims year to date, that's the lowest in the CompSAT history.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: The borough of Brooklyn and the borough of Queens are the lowest shooting victims on record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Just looking at overall crime in the city, we're down 6.2%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: That's down 5,000 fewer index crimes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We're down in five of the seven categories.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: The Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: The Bronx is leading the way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Down 11.9%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: That's almost 2,500 crimes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Bronx South is down 16.3%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Bronx North is down 7.3%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So a major success.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: And what we've done in the Bronx is we've created two patrol boroughs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: What that means, more cops, more specialty units, more resources, more executive leadership and oversight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: And it's delivering on equity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: The borough of Brooklyn, the borough of Manhattan, and the borough of Queens all have two patrol boroughs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Now it's time for the Bronx to get their fair share and make the neighborhood safer up in the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: And we look at the results in the Bronx, we've had some positive results on our investment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: The Bronx as a whole is leading the entire city in major crime decline.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: In Bronx North,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We've seen declines in major crime overall, in auto theft, in grand larceny, in robberies, and in burglaries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So I want to highlight the success in the Bronx North.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So what do we...

chapters.summary: Feliz asks about remaining challenges on shootings and murders. Hout explains the department's all-department approach using mobile field forces of ~40 officers that can be rapidly deployed to shooting hotspots.
chapters.title: Feliz asks about remaining challenges on shootings and murders

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: No, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: You could finish if you...

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: What would you say are some of the challenges that we continue to face when it comes to shootings and murders?

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: We've made progress.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: What are some of the challenges that prevent us from taking that progress even further, if any?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So when we look at shootings, I want to just start in the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: When we look at the Bronx as a whole,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: where we do see shootings and homicides are down in the Bronx leading the major crime and decline, anytime there's a shooting in the Bronx or any patrol borough, we follow the data.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We take an all department approach, looking to see where we can increase deployment and add resources.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: And we're very nimble on how we do that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: You know, if we need to take extra resources and move them, we'll use a mobile field force.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: And a mobile field force, just to explain what that is, it's about 40 police officers, five sergeants, two lieutenants, and a captain.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: And they can be moved into any area that we need, and they can be placed where we need them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: That's on top of already increased deployment.

chapters.summary: Feliz asks about factors driving down robberies and burglaries to near-historic lows. Hout explains the data-driven approach of analyzing where robberies and burglaries occur and precisely deploying officers accordingly.
chapters.title: Feliz asks about robbery and burglary decline strategies

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Talk to us about the robberies and the burglaries.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Those numbers are all sold down compared to last year, and they're almost at historic lows.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Not at historic lows, but almost at historic lows.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: What are factors and policies and crime policing strategies that have played a role when it comes to bringing down the robberies and the burglaries at the numbers they are?

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So when we look at robberies and burglaries, again, we look at the data.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We look at where they're happening.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We look at who's committing them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We look at where we could precisely deploy to combat any future robberies or burglaries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: And again, that can change as needed.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: What would you say are the top three crime reduction strategies that have had the greatest measurable impact on the decline in major crime?

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I know you mentioned CompStat.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: What are other policies and rules that you've been able to run?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So we deployed to our summer zones, and like I said, it's not by accident.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We're down in six of the seven categories, as well as shootings, shooting victims, and confirmed shots fired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut

chapters.summary: Gerber emphasizes that NYPD strategies are interconnected—CompStat, deployment, summer zones, crew takedowns, and pattern analysis all work together. He credits Commissioner Tisch with breaking down silos between detective, patrol, intel, and crime control units.
chapters.title: Gerber on interconnected strategies and breaking down silos under Commissioner Tisch

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And Chair, I think an important point, you were asking about strategies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: I think the strategies intersect, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: They're interconnected, and that's really important.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: So we talk about deployment, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Precision deployment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: We talk about the summer zones.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: We talk about CompStat as a means of holding commanders accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: You know, we talk about the looking at robbery patterns and burglary patterns.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: We talk about the crew takedowns, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: These things, part of what's so important is these things are not siloed, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: It's, you know, through CompStat, looking at data, making sure that decisions are data-driven when it comes to deployment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: Adjusting the summer violence zones as necessary in light of that data, seeing how the crew activity and crew takedowns are going to intersect with what we're seeing, whether in the summer violence zones or otherwise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: There are these different strategies, yes, but the point is that they're all interconnected.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And actually, I think a really important thing also is

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: And I think this is something that we've made a lot of progress on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: particularly under Commissioner Tisch, is that things not be siloed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michael Gerber
utterances.text: No, it's everything interconnected, working and breaking down any of those silos because it's one team working towards one goal.

chapters.summary: Feliz notes most crime categories remain drastically up compared to pre-pandemic 2017-2019, with 21,500 felony assaults this year versus 15,000 in 2019. He asks Hout to define felony assault and explain the challenges.
chapters.title: Feliz on pre-pandemic crime comparison and felony assault definition

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Okay, speaking about trends, we've obviously made a lot of progress.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Again, murders and shootings are at historic lows.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: The robberies and the burglaries, they also seem to be at nearly historic lows.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: And also, most of the numbers are down compared to last year.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: But the numbers still seem to be drastically up compared to the pre-COVID years, specifically 2017, 18, and 19.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Crime was very low before the pandemic, and it seems like it skyrocketed during the pandemic, and it seems like we still haven't been able to bring it down to those very safe years, 2017, 18, and 19.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Not only did we brought down the shootings and the murders, but it seems like most of the other crime categories are still up compared to the pre-pandemic years.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: So some questions about that, and specifically felony assaults.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: So this year we've had year to date 21.5 thousand felony assaults, for example, versus 15,000 year to date in 2019.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: First, tell us what is a felony assault, just so that we could all be clear.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: About what type of crime we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: What is a felony assault?

chapters.summary: Hout explains felony assault covers serious physical injury, assaults on elderly and public service workers. He details 80% arrest rate, 40% domestic violence cases with 92% arrest rate, and 50% increase in assaults on public employees. NYPD has 450 dedicated DV investigators.
chapters.title: Hout on felony assault breakdown, domestic violence, and public employee assaults

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: And talk to us about some of the challenges.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So felony assault is a very serious crime.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: It's an elderly person getting assaulted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: It's a serious physical injury.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: It's a police officer getting assaulted, a public service worker getting assaulted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So we take it extremely seriously.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So looking at felony assaults, felony assaults is a top priority for this department.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Our closure rates highlight how serious we take this issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Felony assaults are slightly up this year and have been increasing for the past several years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: However, the department is playing its part.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Citywide, the NYPD has made roughly 80% of arrests on all felony complaints.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: That's an all-time high.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: To put that in perspective, that's 17,000 arrests.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: This is a direct result of great patrol response, detective bureau gathering evidence, supporting survivors, and working with all our prosecuting partners.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We can't do it alone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We cannot do it alone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: And we are working with the Avis groups, with the district attorney's office, and all our partners.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: And when we go even deeper, we look at two main drivers for felony assaults.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: The first is domestic violence, and that's nearly 40% of felony assaults.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: And assaults on public sector employees, that's up 50% from last year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So for domestic violence, NYPD has made arrests on roughly 92% of these complaints.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: Again, that's no accident.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: We have over 450 dedicated investigators assigned to domestic violence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: What that means is when a victim of domestic violence reports the crime,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: when they walk in, when they call 911, that investigator is going to be with them from the inception.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: And they're going to deal with them through the complaint, through the court process, through the arrest process, so they feel comfortable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So they're not telling that story many times to a different investigator.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: It's just easier and it makes them feel safe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: So that's what we're doing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: With public sector employees, the department is dedicated to significant resources in investigating and holding these perpetrators accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: These are our city nurses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Haut
utterances.text: These are our teachers, our MTA employees who work alongside with us, and they're getting assaulted, and we want to bring justice for them.

utterances.text: Can you provide some raw numbers on that?
